observation.visible_scene: A clear glass jar filled with a translucent yellow liquid sits on a white circular base against a mauve wall that carries the jar's cast shadow on the left. A vertical metal shaft protrudes from the bottom center of the jar (a faint translucent blade/propeller shape is partly visible near it). Suspended in the liquid is a pale cream/white solid mass, and a thick white foam layer floats at the top surface at the start. The camera and the jar are stationary throughout; the background, shadow and base positions do not change.
visible_changes: The white mass in the liquid continuously changes shape and orientation from frame to frame, appearing to spin/deform around the central shaft (it looks like a downward funnel/cone in early frames and a more compact rounded blob in later frames).
The white foam layer on the top surface gradually thins and is gone by roughly the middle-to-late part of the clip (around frames 25-30 onward the surface is just clear yellow liquid).
The overall volume of the suspended white mass appears to shrink over the segment, becoming smaller and more concentrated near the shaft by the last frames.
The yellow liquid level and the jar, base, shaft, wall and shadow remain fixed in position; only the internal mass and surface foam change.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the mixing/stirring was already running before this crop and continues after it (both ends are arbitrary boundaries).
What the white mass and the yellow liquid actually are, and what drives the shaft (no operator or motor is visible).
Whether the mass fully dissolves/incorporates or re-coalesces after the clip ends.
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the motion of the white mass (true rotation around the shaft vs. deformation) is hard to confirm because the jar curvature, reflections and the translucent liquid obscure it.
The blade/propeller at the bottom is only partially and faintly visible through refraction, so its shape and whether it moves are uncertain.
The apparent shrinkage of the white mass could be partly due to foam collapse and changing lighting rather than pure loss of material.
